Package org.apache.juneau.console.views

Class Column

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.console.views.Column
public final class Column extends Object
One datatable column's search configuration — its value SearchType and the optional per-column SearchOperatorSet.
Operator gating

A column's offerable operators are modeled by a single SearchOperatorSet, never a string allow-list or a separate custom-operator map. A custom operator is simply a SearchOperator placed inside a set via SearchOperatorSet.standard(), SearchOperatorSet.with(SearchOperator), or SearchOperatorSet.of(SearchOperator...).

  • Set absent (default): the column offers the entire type-applicable standard universe (or, when resolved against a table, the table-level set — see ViewDef).
  • Set present (operators(SearchOperatorSet)): the column's set entirely replaces the table-level set for this column; the effective operators are that set's type-applicable members.

An operator not on the effective set is a reject (the popup marks it invalid), never a silent rewrite — see offers(String).

Mutability

Deliberately mutable, like ViewDef and RegionDef: a Column is a server-side authoring bean built up once via fluent setters while constructing a view definition, not an immutable value object. Callers must not mutate one concurrently from more than one thread, and must not reuse one across requests unless every request treats it as read-only after construction.

Example:

// A searchable "status" column offering only $eq and $in, plus a custom "$mine" operator. Column status = Column.create("status") .label("Status") .searchType(SearchType.ID) .operators(SearchOperatorSet.of( SearchOperatorSet.standard().get("$eq"), SearchOperatorSet.standard().get("$in"), SearchOperator.create("$mine", "Assigned to me").types(SearchType.ID).build()));

      public Column defaultVisible(boolean v)

      A false value only hides the column when the client's columnConfig (juneau-config.js) is on; without it the column stays visible.

    • toCatalogMap

      public JsonMap toCatalogMap()
      Builds this column's catalog entry: key and label plus the display (render, href, className, defaultVisible) and search (searchType, searchOperators, customOperators) metadata, flattened onto one entry, in the form the datatables card type resolves.

      searchOperators is a list of operator names and customOperators a list of {name,help} maps for the custom ones. Both are emitted only when this column has its own operator set; a column inheriting the table-level set emits just searchType, and a column with no search type emits neither. See toCatalogMap(SearchOperatorSet) to resolve the table-level set into the entry.

      label falls back to name() when unset. A column with an href and no render emits render as the linked renderer.

      Returns:
      The catalog entry.

    • toCatalogMap

      public JsonMap toCatalogMap(SearchOperatorSet tableDefault)
      Builds this column's catalog entry like toCatalogMap(), but emits the column's effective operator set: its own set if it has one, else tableDefault.

      This is how a table-level set reaches the datatables card type, which reads operators per column. With no column set and a null tableDefault, only searchType is emitted.

      Parameters:
      tableDefault - The table-level operator set inherited by a column with none of its own. Can be null.
      Returns:
      The catalog entry.

    • searchMeta

      public static JsonMap searchMeta(String name, String searchTypeWire, List<String> operatorAllowList, List<Map<String,String>> customOperators)
      Builds the per-column search block for the VIEW_META wire contract directly from author-catalog inputs, without the caller having to touch the search-engine beans.

      This is the entry point the chrome/authoring layer uses: it takes only the wire token, the optional allowed-operator names, and the custom operators as plain {name,help} maps — so a chrome-only module that must not depend on the search engine can still emit a column's search block by calling here. Internally this builds a single SearchOperatorSet: an allow-list becomes SearchOperatorSet.of(SearchOperator...) with exactly the named operators (customs preferred over same-named built-ins), while an absent allow-list becomes SearchOperatorSet.standard() with each custom appended via SearchOperatorSet.with(SearchOperator).

      Parameters:
      name - The column name (row-data key). Must not be null or blank.
      searchTypeWire - The wire SearchType token, or null.
      operatorAllowList - The explicit allowed-operator names, or null for the default (the full type-applicable universe).
      customOperators - Per-column custom operators as {name,help} maps; may be null or empty.
      Returns:
      The {type, operators:[...]} block, or null when searchTypeWire names no known type (a non-searchable column emits no search block).

    • searchMeta

      public JsonMap searchMeta()
      Serializes this column's effective search configuration to the VIEW_META search block: the wire SearchType token plus one entry per effective operator, each carrying the metadata the header popup renders.

      help is present only for custom operators; the popup supplies built-in help text from juneau-search.js.

      Returns:
      The {type, operators:[{name,help,minArgs,maxArgs,combinator,custom}]} block, or null if this column is not searchable.
